verdict.root_cause: Frontend is the reporter, not the source. Its checkout-path gRPC calls fail at TCP connection establishment against the cart service endpoint, with the connection actively refused rather than timing out or being silently dropped [tr_450ceffdcf69]. An active refusal on a concrete reachable IP:port means DNS and routing worked and nothing was listening, i.e. the cartservice process was down or crash-looping across essentially the whole queried window (failures at both ~05:35:46 and ~06:07:28). This also explains why frontend and checkoutservice show no step change: the fault predates the 'baseline' window and touches only the checkout sub-path, so aggregates stay bursty and flat [tr_d7e2241f381a, tr_d3bf0de7c817]. Why cartservice stopped listening is unestablished — no dispatch touched cartservice, the trace backend was itself 503 [tr_f5a6ef9c0b22], and all change-log queries began at onset and ran forward, missing the pre-onset window [tr_4db2c8ec3bc5, tr_f8a264b7f48e, tr_3d861d8a754e].
verdict.reasoning: The only positive directional signal is the frontend log evidence: outbound gRPC client stacks, a refused TCP dial to the cart endpoint, and error details naming cart retrieval on the checkout path [tr_450ceffdcf69]. That excludes frontend-local faults, latency/deadline shapes, application 5xx, DNS failure, and silent filtering. Connection refused is the signature of no listener — a dead process, not a slow one, which is why dependency_latency does not fit. The flat metric comparisons corroborate rather than contradict: sd exceeds mean and baseline and incident maxima are identical in both services, consistent with the outage already spanning the reference period [tr_d7e2241f381a, tr_d3bf0de7c817]. checkoutservice alerting last and having an empty change log fits propagation toward the caller [tr_f8a264b7f48e]. I withhold fault_class because the classes differ precisely where no dispatch looked: an OOM kill, an unstartable artifact, and a listener bound to the wrong port all present to a caller as connection refused.
open_questions: cartservice itself was never queried — its logs, change history, restart/OOMKill counts and readiness state would settle fault_class in one dispatch.
No change-log query covered the pre-onset period; every window started at the incident timestamp and ran forward.
Whether cartservice is fully down or flapping, and why frontend's error ratio is only ~7% if the cart path is hard-failing throughout.

alternatives.root_cause: cartservice is crash-looping on a bad artifact or unstartable build, so no listener is ever established.
alternatives.why_not: Plausible and would produce identical connection-refused symptoms, but no change record for cartservice was retrieved either way, and the pre-onset change window was never queried — this is speculation about a mechanism nobody measured.

alternatives.root_cause: cartservice is being killed for exceeding a memory or connection limit and restarts into the same condition.
alternatives.why_not: Equally consistent with refused connections, but no cartservice resource metrics, OOM events or restart counts were gathered, so nothing distinguishes it from the deploy or config explanations.

alternatives.root_cause: cartservice is running but bound to a different port or address than the one frontend dials, so the expected endpoint refuses.
alternatives.why_not: The refusal names a specific internal address and port, which is compatible with a binding mismatch, but a stable long-lived misconfiguration would not normally coincide with a fresh critical alert, and no config evidence for cartservice exists.

proposal.expected_effect: Recreating the cartservice container should put a listener back on 172.18.0.15:7070. Observable as: (1) frontend logs stop emitting the `14 UNAVAILABLE: No connection established` / `connection refused` pairs on the GetCart-in-checkout path within a minute or two of the recreate — the same LogQL selector `{service="frontend"}` that produced tr_450ceffdcf69 should go quiet on that specific error shape; (2) frontend's aggregate error ratio (the tr_d7e2241f381a query) settling at or below its ~0.054 baseline mean rather than the ~0.073 incident mean. Note the second signal is weak on its own — the shift it must undo is only 1.36x on a series whose sd exceeds its mean — so the log-line cessation is the primary confirmation and the metric is corroborating only.
proposal.if_wrong: Falsified if, after the recreate, frontend still logs connection-refused against the cart endpoint — that means cartservice is crash-looping on start (bad image, bad config, OOM, failed dependency), and a plain restart cannot fix a service that will not stay up. Also falsified if the refusals stop but frontend's error ratio does not move at all, which would mean the ~7% error floor was never the cart path and the checkout failures are a small slice of unrelated bursty errors. Two known holes make this a medium-confidence proposal rather than a high one: cartservice itself was never queried (no logs, no restart/OOMKill count, no readiness state), and no change-log query covered the pre-onset window, so a pre-incident deploy or config edit to cartservice remains entirely unexamined. Those same gaps are why rollback_image and revert_config are not proposed — their preconditions require a prior tag or config recorded in change history for this service, and no query has established one. If a single dispatch against cartservice is cheaper than an irreversible recreate, do that first: it would settle fault_class and might redirect this to rollback_image.
proposal.risk: The recreate is irreversible and destroys the evidence of why cartservice stopped listening — in-container logs, exit codes, and crash state go with it, and the open question 'was it down or flapping, and why' may become permanently unanswerable. In-process state is discarded; for this world's cartservice that is cache only, but any carts held in process rather than in the backing store are lost, which users experience as emptied carts. If the true cause is a bad image or config change that landed before the incident window, the restart brings the same broken process back and burns the diagnostic state for nothing. If cartservice is currently flapping rather than fully down, the recreate also resets whatever restart-backoff counter exists and can mask the flap for a while.
proposal.blast_radius: cartservice only, for the duration of the recreate. Inbound callers named in the graph: frontend (direct) and, transitively, checkoutservice via the checkout path — both see connection resets during the recreate, which is a strict no-op for them if the endpoint is already refusing connections. loadgenerator's checkout transactions are the user-visible surface. No other service in the incident set (adservice, productcatalogservice, recommendationservice, currencyservice, paymentservice, shippingservice, emailservice, accountingservice) calls cartservice and none should observe a change; if any of them shifts behaviour after this, the dependency graph used here is wrong.

triage_judgement.reasoning: Critical multi-service alerting on frontend and checkout within seconds, spanning the user-facing path; nothing here can be dismissed and no open incident covers it.
